meta.name: PhysAlts STEM Atlas — Chemistry, Materials, Earth/Climate & Engineering Hubs
meta.description: 42 verified global flagship laboratories, universities, and industrial research centers across chemistry & materials science (11), earth/ocean/climate sciences (11), and semiconductors, robotics & aerospace engineering (20).

hubs.name: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society
hubs.summary: Historic physical chemistry institute in Berlin-Dahlem leading heterogeneous catalysis, ultrafast surface physics, ab-initio electronic structure theory (FHI-aims), and cold-molecule spectroscopy.
hubs.nobel: Nobel laureates include Gerhard Ertl (2007 Chemistry, surface catalysis), Ernst Ruska (1986 Physics, electron microscope), Max von Laue, and Fritz Haber.

stages.highschool: Explore Berlin-Dahlem's historic chemistry trail and Long Night of the Sciences open labs.
stages.undergrad: Student research assistantships in surface science, electrocatalysis, and computational chemistry.
stages.masters: MSc thesis placements affiliated with FU Berlin, HU Berlin, and TU Berlin.
stages.phd: IMPRS for Elementary Processes in Physical Chemistry fully funded doctoral fellowships.
stages.postdoc: Max Planck and Alexander von Humboldt Postdoctoral Fellowships in green catalysis and ultrafast lasers.
stages.assoc_prof: Independent Research Group Leader awards advancing CO2-to-fuel electrochemistry.
stages.prof: Max Planck Director chairs uniting physical chemistry with FAIRMAT open materials data.

rabbitLinks.reason: Operates ultrafast X-ray spectroscopy experiments at DESY's PETRA III and European XFEL to film chemical reactions live.
Surface catalysis discoveries by Gerhard Ertl solved the atomic mechanism of the industrial Haber-Bosch ammonia process.

projects.name: NOMAD / FAIRMAT Open Materials Data & FHI-aims

hubs.name: Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung
hubs.summary: Despite its historic 1912 name ('Coal Research'), today one of the world's premier pure catalysis institutes—birthplace of Fischer-Tropsch chemistry, Ziegler-Natta polymerization, and Nobel-winning asymmetric organocatalysis.
hubs.nobel: Karl Ziegler (1963 Chemistry Nobel, polyethylene catalysis) and Benjamin List (2021 Chemistry Nobel, asymmetric organocatalysis).

stages.highschool: Learn how tiny metal-free organic catalysts replace toxic heavy metals in drug synthesis.
stages.undergrad: Summer research placements in organic synthesis, homogeneous catalysis, and ORCA quantum chemistry.
stages.masters: MSc theses with Ruhr University Bochum, University of Duisburg-Essen, and RWTH Aachen.
stages.phd: IMPRS for Sustainable Catalysis (SusCat) fully funded PhD fellowships.
stages.postdoc: Postdoctoral fellowships in organocatalysis, mechanochemistry, and quantum chemistry (ORCA).
stages.assoc_prof: Independent Group Leaders developing sustainable catalytic pathways for green chemistry.
stages.prof: Max Planck Directors advancing metal-free catalysis and zero-carbon synthetic chemistry.

rabbitLinks.reason: Combines quantum-chemical catalysis benchmarks with Meta FAIR's Open Catalyst graph neural networks.
Shared mission in elegant, green molecular synthesis alongside click chemistry.

projects.name: Asymmetric Organocatalysis & ORCA Quantum Chemistry Suite

hubs.name: Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research
hubs.summary: Global center for soft-matter physics and synthetic macromolecules—pioneering bottom-up graphene nanoribbons, organic electronics, multiscale molecular simulations, and bio-inspired smart polymers.
hubs.nobel: World leader in molecularly precise nanographenes, organic photovoltaics, and coarse-grained polymer physics.

stages.highschool: Explore Mainz science outreach on biodegradable smart polymers and flexible solar films.
stages.undergrad: Summer internships in macromolecular chemistry, laser spectroscopy, and soft-matter simulation.
stages.masters: MSc projects with Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and TU Darmstadt.
stages.phd: Max Planck Graduate Center (MPGC) interdisciplinary PhDs bridging physics and chemistry.
stages.postdoc: Postdoctoral fellowships in quantum nanocarbons, water interfaces, and neuromorphic polymers.
stages.assoc_prof: Independent Research Group Leader roles in sustainable circular plastics.
stages.prof: Max Planck Director chairs uniting precision synthesis with statistical mechanics.

rabbitLinks.reason: 45 minutes along the Rhine; collaborates on circular polymer recycling and organic semiconductors.
Co-advances atomically precise graphene nanoribbons for future quantum and nanoelectronic circuits.

projects.name: Precision Nanographenes & Sustainable Soft Matter

hubs.name: Beckman Institute at Caltech
hubs.summary: Caltech's interdisciplinary chemistry and biological-instrumentation powerhouse—home to femtochemistry, directed evolution of enzymes, automated DNA sequencing invention, and artificial photosynthesis.
hubs.nobel: Caltech Chemistry & Chemical Engineering boasts Frances Arnold (2018), Robert Grubbs (2005), Ahmed Zewail (1999), Rudolph Marcus (1992), and Linus Pauling.

stages.highschool: Learn how Frances Arnold uses artificial evolution to engineer novel enzymes for green chemistry.
stages.undergrad: Caltech SURF (Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowships) open to Caltech and external students.

hubs.name: MIT Chemistry & Materials Science (DMSE)
hubs.summary: Unites MIT Chemistry and Materials Science & Engineering—birthplace of colloidal quantum dots, next-generation lithium and solid-state batteries, high-temperature superconducting magnets, and AI-guided autonomous synthesis.
hubs.nobel: Moungi Bawendi won the 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for quantum dots; Richard Schrock won the 2005 Nobel in Chemistry.

stages.undergrad: MIT UROP and MSRP (MIT Summer Research Program) in quantum dots, batteries, and nanomaterials.
stages.masters: SM / PhD research tracks in Materials Science, Chemistry, and MIT Energy Initiative (MITEI).

stages.assoc_prof: Collaborative grants with Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) on REBCO superconducting tapes.
stages.prof: Institute chairs pioneering zero-carbon steel, grid batteries, and precision chemical biology.

rabbitLinks.reason: MIT materials and magnet science enabled the high-temperature REBCO superconducting magnets behind SPARC fusion.

hubs.name: Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge
hubs.summary: Three-century-old chemistry powerhouse on Lensfield Road—where Shankar Balasubramanian & David Klenerman invented Solexa/Illumina next-generation DNA sequencing and Clare Grey revolutionized solid-state battery NMR.
hubs.nobel: Associated with 7 Chemistry Nobel Prizes (incl. Lord Todd, John Pople, Gregory Winter, Venki Ramakrishnan) plus the 2020 Millennium Technology Prize for NGS DNA sequencing.

stages.highschool: Compete in the Cambridge Chemistry Challenge (C3L6) run directly by the department.
stages.undergrad: Cambridge Natural Sciences Tripos (Chemistry track) with lab synthesis and quantum chemistry.
stages.masters: MPhil in Chemistry and Part III Chemistry intensive research year.
stages.phd: Fully funded PhD tracks in battery materials (Faraday Institution), atmospheric chemistry, and AI force fields.
stages.postdoc: Herchel Smith and Royal Society University Research Fellowships in Cambridge.
stages.assoc_prof: Principal Investigator groups pioneering machine-learned interatomic potentials (MACE).
stages.prof: Historic 1702 Professorship of Chemistry and interdisciplinary Maxwell Centre leadership.

rabbitLinks.reason: Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis invented right here on Lensfield Road slashed human genome costs from $100M to under $200.

hubs.name: Kyoto University iCeMS (Cell-Material Sciences)
hubs.summary: Japan's flagship WPI institute fusing porous materials chemistry with living cell biology—led by MOF pioneer Susumu Kitagawa (2025 Chemistry Nobel laureate) and closely linked to Shinya Yamanaka's iPS cell institute.
hubs.nobel: Distinguished Professor Susumu Kitagawa won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (with Richard Robson & Omar Yaghi) for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs); co-founded with 2012 Medicine laureate Shinya Yamanaka.

stages.undergrad: Kyoto University international undergraduate summer research exchanges.

hubs.name: Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics (CAS DICP)
hubs.summary: China's premier institute for catalytic chemistry, solar hydrogen, vanadium flow batteries, and extreme-ultraviolet molecular dynamics (operating the Dalian Coherent Light Source free-electron laser).
hubs.nobel: Pioneered single-atom catalysis (Tao Zhang), industrial methanol-to-olefins (DMTO), and megawatt-scale grid flow batteries.

stages.undergrad: Summer research camps in chemical physics, energy storage, and analytical chemistry.

stages.postdoc: DICP International Postdoctoral Fellowships with access to the Dalian Coherent Light Source.
stages.assoc_prof: Principal Investigator groups linking molecular beam physics to industrial clean energy.

hubs.name: BASF Global Research & Verbund Site
hubs.summary: The world's largest integrated chemical research complex (~10 sq km along the Rhine), where Carl Bosch scaled ammonia synthesis to feed half the planet and modern R&D pioneers electrified furnaces, battery cathodes, and chemical recycling.
hubs.nobel: Carl Bosch won the 1931 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for high-pressure industrial chemical methods (Haber-Bosch process).

stages.highschool: Visit BASF Kids' Lab and explore circular chemistry and electrochemistry demonstrations.
stages.undergrad: Industrial chemistry and chemical engineering internships in Ludwigshafen.
stages.masters: MSc theses in process engineering, polymer science, and AI molecular formulation.
stages.phd: BASF PhD collaborations (including Joint Research Network on Advanced Materials with KIT/Heidelberg).

stages.assoc_prof: Academic research partnerships via BASF's Joint Research Network (JONAS / CARA).
stages.prof: Strategic collaborations decarbonizing global chemical manufacturing (e-Furnace / methane pyrolysis).

rabbitLinks.reason: Historical partnership with Fritz Haber scaled catalytic nitrogen fixation into the modern fertilizer industry.
Just 20 km across the Rhine from Heidelberg—uniting industrial chemistry with molecular life sciences.

hubs.name: Corning Sullivan Park Research Center
hubs.summary: One of America's oldest industrial materials laboratories—inventor of low-loss optical fiber (1970, enabling the global fiber-optic internet), Pyrex borosilicate glass, catalytic converter ceramics, Gorilla Glass, and telescope mirror blanks.
hubs.nobel: Robert Maurer, Donald Keck, and Peter Schultz invented low-loss optical fiber here in 1970 (National Medal of Technology & Innovation).

stages.highschool: Visit the Corning Museum of Glass Innovation Center to explore fiber optics and glass physics.
stages.undergrad: Corning Research & Development summer internships in glass science, ceramics, and photonics.
stages.masters: Optical physics and materials process engineering roles in Upstate New York.
stages.phd: Corning Graduate Research Fellowship and Science & Technology research scientist positions.
stages.postdoc: Materials Scientist roles in fusion-drawn ultrathin glass, hollow-core fiber, and EUV optics.
stages.assoc_prof: Academic collaborations with Alfred University, Cornell University, and Penn State.
stages.prof: Joint glass-physics and optical-communications consortia for AI data center interconnects.

rabbitLinks.reason: Located 45 miles from Ithaca; Corning's low-loss optical fibers carry the global internet's data between AI clusters.
Corning's ultra-low-expansion glass substrates and optical materials are critical to precision semiconductor lithography and space telescopes.

hubs.name: The Molecular Foundry (Lawrence Berkeley National Lab)
hubs.summary: US Department of Energy open nanoscience user facility high in the Berkeley hills—providing free peer-reviewed access to atomic-resolution electron microscopes (NCEM), automated robotic synthesis, and LBNL's Materials Project.
hubs.nobel: Adjacent to LBNL's 16 Nobel Prizes; home to the Materials Project open crystal database powering global AI materials discovery (GNoME, MatterGen).

stages.highschool: Explore the open Materials Project web app to inspect 150,000+ computed crystal structures.
stages.undergrad: DOE SULI (Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internships) at Berkeley Lab.
stages.masters: Research placements in nanoscale fabrication, 2D quantum materials, and robotic chemistry.

stages.postdoc: Molecular Foundry & Alvarez Postdoctoral Fellowships uniting nanoscience with NERSC supercomputing.
stages.assoc_prof: User Executive Committee collaborations across all 7 nanoscale research facilities.

hubs.name: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI)
hubs.summary: The world's largest independent ocean research organization—operator of the deep-diving submersible HOV Alvin (6,500 m), discoverer of deep-sea hydrothermal vents and RMS Titanic, and pioneer of autonomous underwater robotics.
hubs.nobel: Discovered chemosynthetic deep-sea hydrothermal vent ecosystems (1977), reshaping our search for life on icy ocean worlds like Europa and Enceladus.

stages.highschool: Explore WHOI's Dive and Discover virtual deep-sea expeditions and Ocean Twilight Zone portal.
stages.undergrad: WHOI Summer Student Fellowship (10–12 week paid Cape Cod oceanography & marine robotics fellowship).
stages.masters: MIT-WHOI Joint Program in Oceanography / Applied Ocean Science & Engineering.
stages.phd: MIT-WHOI Joint PhD Program — world's flagship oceanography & marine engineering doctorate.
stages.postdoc: WHOI Postdoctoral Scholar Fellowship (18-month independent awards).
stages.assoc_prof: Chief Scientist leadership aboard research vessels R/V Atlantis and R/V Neil Armstrong.
stages.prof: Global leadership in Ocean Observatories Initiative, Atlantic overturning (AMOC), and ocean-world astrobiology.

hubs.name: Scripps Institution of Oceanography (UC San Diego)
hubs.summary: Pacific coast powerhouse of ocean, atmospheric, and planetary science—home of the iconic Keeling Curve (continuous Mauna Loa CO2 monitoring since 1958), Argo global ocean-float network, and atmospheric-river forecasting.
hubs.nobel: Charles David Keeling established the modern atmospheric CO2 record here; Mario Molina (1995 Chemistry Nobel) and Walter Munk shaped climate & ocean physics.

stages.highschool: Track live daily atmospheric CO2 readings via the Scripps Keeling Curve portal.
stages.undergrad: Scripps Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF) — 9-week paid La Jolla research program.
stages.masters: MS in Marine Biology, Climate Science and Policy, or Oceanography at UC San Diego.
stages.phd: Fully funded PhD spanning physical oceanography, geophysics, polar glaciology, and marine chemistry.
stages.postdoc: Scripps Institutional Postdoctoral Fellowships sailing aboard R/V Roger Revelle and R/V Sally Ride.
stages.assoc_prof: Principal Investigator tracks in the global 4,000-float Argo Ocean Observing Array.
stages.prof: Leadership across IPCC assessments, Pacific climate dynamics, and marine robotics.

hubs.summary: Housed in I.M. Pei's iconic Mesa Lab against the Colorado Flatirons, stewarding the Community Earth System Model (CESM), WRF weather prediction model, solar-terrestrial physics, and the Derecho climate supercomputer.
hubs.nobel: NCAR scientists contributed core climate projections honored in the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the IPCC.

hubs.name: ECMWF (European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts)
hubs.summary: Intergovernmental benchmark for global numerical weather prediction across Reading, Bologna (HPC supercomputer), and Bonn—producer of the ERA5 climate reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Service, Destination Earth, and AIFS AI weather model.
hubs.nobel: ERA5 reanalysis is the single most important open dataset behind the entire AI weather forecasting revolution (GraphCast, GenCast, FourCastNet, AIFS).

stages.highschool: Explore live Copernicus Climate Pulse global temperature and ocean heat dashboards.
stages.undergrad: ECMWF Summer of Weather Code (ESoWC) open-source mentorships for students and developers.

stages.assoc_prof: Co-developing Destination Earth (DestinE) kilometer-scale climate digital twins.
